items.title: Gold subdued with spotlight on US inflation data
items.summary: Gold prices have seen a slight retreat as investors brace for key US inflation figures that could sway interest rates. The robust US dollar further complicates matters, making gold pricier for overseas buyers. While the Federal Reserve is poised to maintain current rates this month, market watchers are speculating on a potential hike in December.

items.title: Bitcoin price prediction: Why BTC USD can drop before a Fed rate hike and rally after
items.summary: Explore the impact of Federal Reserve rate hikes on Bitcoin prices, examining the relationship between interest rates and investor behavior in the crypto market.

items.title: Fed’s Hammack Says Smaller, Frequent Rate Adjustments Preferable
items.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said smaller, more frequent adjustments to policy can help inflation expectations remain anchored, but she stopped short of backing a rate increase this month.

items.title: Rising Bond Yields Are No Excuse for Central Bank Inertia
items.summary: Are the bond and derivatives markets doing the tough work for central bankers? Swaps are pricing a globally coordinated cycle of interest rate increased over the next 12 months, and longer-term bond yields are hitting multi-decade highs in the US, Europe and Japan. items.title: Strong US growth, sticky inflation may prompt two more Fed rate hikes in 2026: BofA
items.summary: Bank of America (BofA) expects the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates twice more this year, in October and December, as resilient economic growth and persistent inflation pressures could require further monetary tightening, even as policymakers consider slowing the pace of rate hikes.

items.title: Dollar stays near 18-month high as Mideast conflict, inflation data in focus
items.summary: The dollar's steadiness reflects a cautious market responding to geopolitical stresses in the Middle East, which have dampened investor confidence. Fluctuations in oil prices continue as conflict in Saudi Arabia disrupts infrastructure, paired with controversial ceasefire news. Investors focus on the looming US consumer price index report, which will influence Federal Reserve interest rate policies.
